docs.text: Why snapshots, native ordering and deferred effects matter IRC objects can disappear as a native callback unwinds. The bridge copies values into owned, bounded snapshots so a retained JavaScript event does not become a dangling native pointer. Text carries both a decoded view and exact bytes; truncation metadata tells the caller when a bounded snapshot is incomplete. Editing a snapshot changes the copy, not the IRC object. Command rewriting is a separately validated API. Native module order still applies. A prior module's decision may prevent another observer from seeing an event, and per-target/core-generated command callbacks may appear more than once. Therefore the hook stream is neither an exactly-once audit log nor proof that another client received a message. Direct synchronous mutations could recurse into the same hooks with partially processed native state. Notices and renames instead queue explicit effects to a safe main-loop point, re-resolve actors/targets, and suppress JS feedback while the effect runs. This avoids unbounded recursion but also means queuing an effect is not a success receipt or transaction. Later native rejection does not retract an already accepted effect; disconnected users may cause it to be skipped. Reload follows the same preference for explicit transitions: construct an entire candidate set first, then replace the active set. This protects the previous state from partial initialization failure, but is not an atomic snapshot of the filesystem. Success resets JavaScript state. The V8 platform remains process-lifetime and NODELETE retains necessary module code; replacing native binaries needs a restart. API reference specifies authority/effect limits; hook reference lists native result semantics and exceptions.
docs.title: Snapshots, ordering and effects

docs.text: Why trusted scripts are not a sandbox The module removes ambient Node APIs: scripts do not receive process , require , filesystem/network APIs or WASI. That narrows the surface, but it does not isolate the IRC daemon from an embedded native engine. V8 or native out-of-memory failure can terminate the process; a watchdog cannot interrupt blocking native code. The old-generation target is not a total process-memory ceiling. Authority describes the bridge's permitted effects, not whether source code is safe to run. User-authority code may affect the triggering local actor; explicitly admin-authorized code may target other local users. An admin file's isolate does not share globals with a lower-authority file. Neither mode is suitable for unreviewed user-supplied programs. JavaScript remains the host language and Wasm participates through explicit JS wrappers. Wasm does not create a separate native hook ABI or hard containment. A separate-process design would be needed for a stronger crash/resource boundary; that redesign is not implemented here. Runtime checks and trusted-source review remain necessary even when the script uses only Wasm exports. The separate precommand debug logger is also not a security boundary. It may log unredacted command data. This module's bridge avoids printing command contents and script exception text, but script snapshots themselves can contain credentials and private messages. Treat access to scripts and retained data as privileged.
docs.title: Trust and containment

docs.text: Build and configure the module Use this guide when adding trusted scripts to an existing InspIRCd 4.12.1 setup. Review trust and containment before enabling it. Build the optional image from the repository root: ~~~sh docker build -f Dockerfile.javascript -t inspircd:javascript . ~~~ Make your script files readable by the daemon user. Put them under your configuration directory, for example scripts/hooks.js . Do not give an IRC user write access to administrator-loaded scripts. Add explicit configuration: ~~~text ~~~ Start a disposable instance with your complete, validated server configuration before changing a live server. In the image the config directory is /inspircd/conf/ and the daemon UID/GID is 10000. Check startup logs for script load errors and exercise the intended hook using synthetic data. Do not enable the unredacted precommand debug logger to debug secrets. For multiple files, use repeated <javascript file="..."> tags or a <javascript directory="scripts/extra" authority="user"> entry. Directory loading is non-recursive; sort order, failures and size limits are in the configuration reference . Grant authority="admin" only to reviewed files needing local cross-user effects; never use it merely to suppress an authorization error.

docs.text: Maintain and publish the documentation Use Python 3.11+ in a virtual environment, from the repository root: python3 -m venv .venv-docs .venv-docs/bin/pip install -r requirements-docs.txt python3 tools/generate_docs_reference.py .venv-docs/bin/mkdocs build --strict .venv-docs/bin/mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8000 Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docker/ (or the URL printed by MkDocs). Stop with Ctrl-C. site/ and the virtual environment are ignored by Git. Reference excerpts and hook/type assets are generated from JAVASCRIPT.md , the reviewed hook inventory and TypeScript declarations. Edit those sources then regenerate; --check detects drift. Put learning steps in tutorials, task procedures in how-to guides, exact behavior in reference, and design rationale in explanation. Do not turn a lesson into a configuration catalogue or hide safety limits only in an explanatory essay. The documentation workflow builds on PRs without publishing. On pushes to master or explicit workflow dispatch it may publish to gh-pages using the repository workflow token. GitHub Pages must use the gh-pages branch root. Dispatch requires the workflow to exist on the default branch; do not merge the module PR merely to publish docs. An administrator can publish a reviewed checkout manually: .venv-docs/bin/mkdocs gh-deploy --strict --message 'Publish JavaScript documentation' Use an ephemeral approved Git credential, not a token in a URL or committed file. This command changes the documentation branch only. Site publication is not an IRC daemon/module deployment, and a successful build alone does not prove Pages is live.

docs.text: Reload scripts and recover from failure Use this guide after modifying an already configured script set. You need the normal administrative access required to rehash your InspIRCd server. Save the changed files and validate their syntax and intended effects in a disposable server. Initialization must register handlers without native mutations. Request the server's normal rehash using your existing operator procedure. Check the m_javascript configuration/runtime log and exercise the affected hook. A successful candidate replaces every script isolate, resetting global state. If initialization fails, repair the candidate configuration/source and rehash again. The previous active set and its existing state remain active. If a running file throws, times out, returns a Promise or an invalid decision, fix its source and perform a successful rehash to re-enable it. Do not assume a disabled decision hook silently permits traffic; consult the failure rules . Do not replace a loaded module binary or V8 library in place. Restart the daemon when changing those binaries. Module unload/reload of the same binary is supported, but is not a filesystem watcher or code deployment mechanism.
docs.title: Reload and recover

docs.text: Test module changes Run from the repository root. Never point integration tests at an existing server configuration. Build the pinned InspIRCd SDK and V8 dependencies before native tests. python3 tools/generate_module_hooks.py --check python3 tests/test_generate_module_hooks.py sh tests/js_bindings.sh sh tests/js_script_loader.sh sh tests/js_runtime.sh The runtime script reports SKIP when matching V8 dependencies are missing; a skip is not a pass. You may supply V8_CXXFLAGS and V8_LDFLAGS for matching libraries. For ABI parity against an inspected SDK: python3 tools/generate_module_hooks.py --check --upstream /path/to/inspircd/include/modules.h The full native suite needs an isolated installation with both m_javascript.so and the test-only m_js_hook_probe.so . The optional Docker build supports --build-arg TEST_HOOK_PROBE=1 for this purpose; never ship that probe in a normal image. INSPIRCD_NATIVE=/path/to/installation sh tests/javascript.sh The probe directly invokes all 75 adapters, checks owned snapshots and decision matrices, then exercises selected real lifecycle/message events. This is not natural-trigger E2E coverage for every hook. Consult the repository's CI coverage for quick checks, sanitizers, Valgrind, fuzzing and label-triggered heavy image runs.
docs.title: Test changes

docs.text: Call a configured WebAssembly asset Use this guide to call a synchronous Wasm export from a JavaScript handler. Copy the repository's examples/javascript/answer.wasm into your configuration directory as scripts/answer.wasm . The adjacent answer.wat documents its i32 answer() export, which returns 42. Configure the asset and your JavaScript file: ~~~text ~~~ Use synchronous compilation and instantiation in scripts/wasm.js : ~~~js const instance = new WebAssembly.Instance( new WebAssembly.Module(ircd.wasm('answer')), {}); ircd.on('preCommand', event => { if (event.command === 'PING' && event.params[0] === 'wasm') return { action: 'pass', command: 'PING', params: [String(instance.exports.answer())] }; }); ~~~ Rehash and send a raw PING :wasm on a disposable server. Expect a PONG ending in 42 . Check load/runtime logs if compilation or execution fails. There is no direct Wasm IRC ABI, implicit import resolution, WASI, network or filesystem API. Supply imports explicitly; calls inherit the script's configured authority and deadline. Async compilation/Promises are unsupported.
docs.title: Use WebAssembly

docs.text: Native API and authority The manifest bindings/inspircd.json generates registration rows, utility TypeScript declarations, and a coverage inventory: python3 tools/generate_js_bindings.py python3 tools/generate_js_bindings.py --check Six audited utility wrappers are implemented: match , matchCIDR , isNick , isChannel , stripColor , and time . Inputs have strict arity/types, copied ownership, and explicit conversions. NUL is rejected for native glob/CIDR functions with NUL-terminated internals. The manifest tracks reviewed declarations, manual-wrapper candidates, exclusions, and pending mutations. It is a systematic allowlist and coverage inventory, not an automatic binding of every function in inspircd.h or the whole SDK . New bindings require explicit conversion, lifetime, effect, and authorization policy plus an implementation and tests. Additional explicit host methods: userById(uuid) returns an owned { id, nick } snapshot or null. notice(targetUuid, text) queues a server notice (maximum 400 UTF-8 bytes). rename(targetUuid, nick) queues a validated nickname change. wasm(name) returns a fresh Uint8Array of a configured asset's bytes. Default authority="user" restricts notice/rename targets to the triggering client. Rename runs ordinary NICK processing as that client, retaining native restrictions. Explicit authority="admin" permits targeting other local users; rename directly invokes the native administrative nickname change after nickname validation. No credential, operator identity, or permission is granted to a user. Queued operations re-resolve the original actor and target UUIDs and skip users who disconnected. Only local targets are changed in this initial API. At most 16 effects can be queued per file/event. All effects for the event are discarded on pre denial/error. Accepted effects run at the main-loop safe point, after the current parser stack unwinds. They may still be skipped/rejected by native checks; queuing is not a success receipt or an atomic transaction, and a later core command rejection does not retract accepted queued effects. Native effects and commands they synchronously trigger do not invoke JS hooks, avoiding unbounded feedback loops; ordinary core/native-module checks still apply. TypeScript assets API declarations , snapshot types , hook declarations , utility declarations . Preserve this directory layout for triple-slash references.

docs.text: Command hooks See examples/javascript/hooks.js and modules/js_api.d.ts . ircd.on('preCommand', event => { if (event.command === 'EXAMPLEPING') return { action: 'pass', command: 'PING', params: ['hello'] }; }); ircd.on('postCommand', event => { if (event.command === 'VERSION') ircd.notice(event.userId, 'Handler result: ' + event.result); }); Register at most 16 callbacks per stage per file during initialization. Callbacks run synchronously in registration order, then file order. Pre callbacks receive owned command/parameter snapshots at validated=false . Post callbacks receive result ( SUCCESS , FAILURE , INVALID ) and loop , matching the native hook. validated is true for the post-handler snapshot. This does not prove delivery to another client. The earlier debug logger still observes validated pre events. Fields are command , params , commandBytes , paramBytes , userId , stage , validated , result , and loop . Valid UTF-8 text becomes JavaScript strings; invalid UTF-8 becomes null in the corresponding text field. Uint8Array fields always preserve exact owned bytes, including invalid UTF-8. Tags, client identity fields, and native pointers are not exposed. Editing an event does not edit IRC state. Snapshot values are unredacted; scripts must handle credentials/private messages appropriately. The bridge itself does not print command contents or script exception text. The separate debug logger does print unredacted contents. Pre return values: undefined or { action: 'pass' } : continue ordinary core processing. { action: 'deny' } : stop processing and discard this event's queued effects. { action: 'pass', command: 'PING', params: ['text'] } : request a rewrite. Rewrite parameters may also be Uint8Array values. Rewrites require uppercase ASCII command tokens, at most 15 parameters, a conservative 510-byte line limit, no NUL/CR/LF, and valid middle-parameter syntax. Lone UTF-16 surrogates are rejected. Unknown/server-only target handlers are rejected. Rewrites are redispatched under the original client through the core parser, including operator/registration checks, rather than invoking a cached handler. Tags are retained internally. This incurs additional core flood accounting. The exact replacement skips a second JS pre pass; nested commands still pass through hooks, with rewrite depth bounded to eight. A later script sees earlier scripts' proposed changes. Other modules may veto before this hook, and unknown commands can reach native pre hooks more than once when another module resolves them. Core-generated commands and per-target post events may also appear. There is no exactly-once or complete-audit guarantee. Post return values are ignored except that Promises are rejected. A post error cannot undo a command that has already executed.
docs.title: Command hooks

docs.text: Configuration docker build -f Dockerfile.javascript -t inspircd:javascript . The optional image uses Alpine 3.22, InspIRCd v4.12.1 by default, and matching nodejs-dev / nodejs-libs 22.23.2-r0. Only V8 APIs are used; no Node environment, process , require , filesystem API, network API, or WASI is installed in scripts. The original Dockerfile stays unchanged and does not enable the extra module. Update both dependency pins together for security updates. The optional Dockerfile checks that the built module links libnode and has the ELF NODELETE flag. Example configuration (files must already exist): <module name="javascript"> <javascriptsettings timeoutms="25"> <javascript file="scripts/hooks.js"> <javascript directory="scripts/extra" authority="user"> <javascript file="scripts/operator.js" authority="admin"> <javascriptwasm name="answer" file="scripts/answer.wasm"> <log method="stdout" level="normal" type="m_javascript"> Relative paths resolve under InspIRCd's configured config directory. Source entries execute in configuration order; direct regular .js files inside each directory execute in bytewise filename order. Subdirectories and discovered symlinks are skipped. Explicit file/directory symlinks are canonicalized. Duplicate canonical source paths, missing/unreadable files, empty matching directories, and oversized sources fail configuration. Defaults are 128 sources, 1 MiB per source, and 16 MiB total; Wasm assets have the same separate limits. Wasm asset names are unique case-sensitive ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen, 1–64 characters; only explicitly configured .wasm files are loaded. Each JavaScript file has its own isolate, global state, and configured authority. Directory authority is inherited by every discovered file. Scripts cannot select or change their authority, share globals with more privileged files, or choose a native execution actor. Scripts are loaded as classic synchronous scripts, not ES modules; no implicit imports, recursive includes, filesystem watching, or timers. Normal InspIRCd rehash loads a complete candidate set with fresh isolates. It replaces the active set only after every file initializes successfully. A failed candidate leaves the previous scripts and their state active. Native mutations are prohibited during initialization. Filesystem reads are bounded but are not a filesystem-wide atomic snapshot. Successful reload resets all JavaScript state.
docs.title: Configuration

Explicit file/directory symlinks are canonicalized. Duplicate canonical source paths, missing/unreadable files, empty matching directories, and oversized sources fail configuration. Defaults are 128 sources, 1 MiB per source, and 16 MiB total; Wasm assets have the same separate limits. Wasm asset names are unique case-sensitive ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen, 1–64 characters; only explicitly configured .wasm files are loaded. Each JavaScript file has its own isolate, global state, and configured authority. Directory authority is inherited by every discovered file. Scripts cannot select or change their authority, share globals with more privileged files, or choose a native execution actor. Scripts are loaded as classic synchronous scripts, not ES modules; no implicit imports, recursive includes, filesystem watching, or timers. Normal InspIRCd rehash loads a complete candidate set with fresh isolates. It replaces the active set only after every file initializes successfully. A failed candidate leaves the previous scripts and their state active. Native mutations are prohibited during initialization. Filesystem reads are bounded but are not a filesystem-wide atomic snapshot. Successful reload resets all JavaScript state.

See the per-hook inventory and modules/js_generated/module_hooks.d.ts for exact names, arguments, native return semantics, and failure policy. Optional modules’ separate EventProvider APIs and native lifecycle methods (Init, ReadConfig, Prioritize, destruction) are not additional script events. Wasm can participate through these JS callbacks; there is no separate Wasm hook ABI. ircd.on("userPreMessage", event => { if (event.details.text.text === "blocked") return {action: "deny"}; }); Except for the existing specialized pre/post-command shape, arguments are owned, bounded snapshots. Strings carry {text, bytes, byteLength, truncated} ; invalid UTF-8 has null text and intact bytes. Lists carry {items, length, truncated} . Snapshots expose no native handles and changing them never changes native state. Text is capped at 64 KiB per value and 256 KiB per event; lists at 256 entries. Each event has stage and nullable userId ; server events may have no actor. User-authority effects require a local actor; explicit admin authority permits local-target effects without an actor. The same queued-effect/reentrancy rules apply to all events. Void hooks observe only; return values are ignored except unsupported Promises. ModResult hooks accept undefined or {action: "pass"} , {action: "deny"} , and (only with admin authority and where inventoried) {action: "allow"} . Allow has the native hook-specific meaning , not a generic permit: consult the inventory/upstream documentation. acceptConnection never accepts allow because it would claim native socket ownership. Hooks run in native module order and an earlier decision can prevent later modules/callbacks from observing an event. Exceptions/timeouts/invalid decisions disable the script until successful rehash. Decision hooks fail closed, except kill, channelPreDelete and userPreQuit pass on failure so cleanup cannot be blocked by a disabled script. Observational failures do not undo native actions. docs.text: Execution and failure limits Script initialization and each file's stage callback batch share its configured wall-clock deadline (default 25 ms, configurable 1–1000 ms). A joined watchdog terminates JavaScript/Wasm execution. A pre exception, timeout, invalid decision, or Promise result rejects the command and disables that file until a successful rehash. Subsequent events needing its callbacks fail closed. A failed post-only file does not block commands through an empty pre stage. Post failures discard that event's queued effects and are reported without script-controlled data. Already-committed effects from earlier events are not rolled back. There are no automatic microtask checkpoints; asynchronous hooks, Promises, and async Wasm compilation are unsupported. Atomics.wait is disabled. Use new WebAssembly.Module(bytes) and new WebAssembly.Instance(module, imports) . Synchronous Wasm compilation/calls run within the same deadline; traps are normal script errors. Each isolate has a 32 MiB old-generation target, not a hard total memory cap. ArrayBuffers/native allocations and process-wide V8 resources are outside it. Total work and memory grow with configured files. Use a small source set; a separate process would be needed for hard resource/crash containment. V8's platform is process-lifetime and never globally disposed/reinitialized on rehash or module reload. ELF NODELETE retains callback/platform code; musl also does not unload DSOs. Per-script handles, watchdogs, contexts, and isolates are cleaned up. Reloading the same module is supported; replacing the module binary or V8 libraries requires restarting the daemon. This module assumes sole ownership of V8 initialization in the process.

docs.text: Your first command hook In this lesson you will run a disposable loopback-only server, rewrite one PING, and observe a notice after VERSION. Use a machine with Docker, Git, and an IRC client that supports raw commands. Do not use a production server. Port 16667 must be free; allow time and disk space for a native V8/InspIRCd build. 1. Get the lesson files and build Run from a fresh checkout (skip cloning if already in this repository): git clone --branch feat/local-echo-command https://github.com/r33drichards/docker.git cd docker docker build -f Dockerfile.javascript -t inspircd:javascript . The optional image contains the module but will load it only because our lesson configuration explicitly requests it. A build must finish successfully before continuing. If a pinned Alpine dependency is unavailable, stop and consult the maintainer rather than substituting mismatched headers and libraries. 2. Start your isolated server docker run -d --name js-lesson --workdir /inspircd -p 127.0.0.1:16667:6667 -v "$PWD/examples/javascript/tutorial:/lab:ro" --entrypoint /inspircd/bin/inspircd inspircd:javascript --nofork --config /lab/inspircd.conf The mount is read-only. The container runs as UID 10000, so the example directory must be traversable and its files readable by that UID. Only host loopback port 16667 is published; no TLS or public networking is set up in this lesson. Follow startup with docker logs -f js-lesson . Wait for normal startup; if the process exits, read its configuration/module error before continuing. 3. Observe the rewritten PING Connect your IRC client to 127.0.0.1:16667 , without TLS, using any new nickname. After registration send a raw IRC command (many clients use /quote ): /quote PING :lesson Expect a server PONG ending in hello-from-javascript instead of lesson . The first callback changed the parameters used by the native command parser. An ordinary /quote PING :unchanged still receives a PONG containing unchanged . 4. Observe the post-command hook /quote VERSION Expect the ordinary VERSION reply and a server NOTICE containing VERSION handler returned SUCCESS . These are separate observations: a native handler result does not prove delivery to another client. Open examples/javascript/tutorial/hooks.js to match each result to its callback. 5. Clean up docker rm -f js-lesson You have registered synchronous callbacks, rewritten a command, and queued a notice. Next, learn to reload scripts safely or look up the command event shape .
